questions.question_text:
A rectangular prism measures $3$ m by $4$ m by $7$ m.
What is its volume in m³?

options.why: Divided the product by $2$ as if the rectangular cross-section were a triangle.
Multiplied $3 \times 7$ and left out the $4$ m dimension.
Added $3 + 4 + 7$ instead of multiplying the dimensions.
Divided by $2$ as if the rectangular cross-section were a triangle.
Used only the $6$ cm and $11$ cm edges, leaving the $5$ cm edge out of the cross-section area.
Added the three dimensions instead of multiplying them.
Used the $10$ mm slant side in place of the $6$ mm perpendicular height.
Left out the $\frac{1}{2}$ when finding the area of the triangular cross-section.
Halved the answer a second time after already using $\frac{bh}{2}$.
Left out the division by $2$ in $A = \frac{h(a+b)}{2}$.
Treated the cross-section as a $9$ m by $4$ m rectangle, ignoring the shorter parallel side.
Treated the cross-section as a $5$ m by $4$ m rectangle, ignoring the longer parallel side.
Divided by $2$ as if the parallelogram cross-section were a triangle.
Stopped at the cross-section area and did not multiply by the $4$ cm depth.
Added the three given dimensions instead of multiplying them.

questions.question_text:
A prism has a trapezium cross-section with parallel sides of $5$ mm and $11$ mm and a perpendicular height of $6$ mm. The prism is $8$ mm long.
What is its volume in mm³?

options.why: Left out the division by $2$ in the trapezium area formula.
Used a rectangle with base $11$ mm and height $6$ mm, ignoring the shorter parallel side.
Used a rectangle with base $5$ mm and height $6$ mm, ignoring the longer parallel side.

questions.question_text:
A skateboard ramp is a triangular prism.
Its cross-section is a right triangle with a base of $3.2$ m and a perpendicular height of $0.9$ m, and the ramp is $2.5$ m wide.
What is the volume of the ramp, in m³, correct to $1$ decimal place?

options.why: Multiplied $3.2 \times 0.9 \times 2.5$ without halving for the triangular cross-section.
Halved the volume a second time after already using $\frac{bh}{2}$.
Added the three given dimensions instead of multiplying them.

questions.question_text:
A vase with a volume of $315$ cm³ is packed into a rectangular box with internal dimensions of $12$ cm by $7.5$ cm by $8$ cm. The space around the vase is filled with packing foam.
What is the volume of foam in cm³?

options.why: Added the vase volume to the box volume instead of subtracting it.
Calculated the box volume but did not subtract the vase volume.
Halved the rectangular box volume before subtracting the vase volume, treating the box as a triangular prism.

questions.question_text:
A prism has a trapezium cross-section whose parallel sides are $3.6$ m and $6.8$ m, measured $2.25$ m apart. The prism is $4.5$ m long.
What is its volume in m³, correct to $2$ decimal places?

options.why: Left out the division by $2$ in the trapezium area formula.
Used only the longer parallel side, calculating $6.8 \times 2.25 \times 4.5$.
Used only the shorter parallel side, calculating $3.6 \times 2.25 \times 4.5$.

questions.question_text:
A cube-shaped tank has an internal side length of $3$ m.
What is its full volume in m³?

options.why: Calculated the square base area but did not multiply by the tank height.
Multiplied the square base area by $2$ instead of the $3$ m height.
Multiplied by the $3$ m side length four times instead of three times.
